input.explanation:
Cause: `average_spend_per_item_this_month` divides the month's total spend by the number of purchases in the current month without checking that the list is non-empty. Any account viewing the account page with no purchases so far this month (the common case early in a month, or for inactive shoppers) makes `len(bought)` zero and raises ZeroDivisionError. While `monthly-spend-feature` was off this code path was never reached; flipping the flag on at 13:40-13:41 exposed it and drove the account-page error rate from ~1% to ~31-37%. The flag flip is not the fault - the unguarded division is.

Fix: guard the divide. With no purchases in the current month there is no per-item average, so the function returns 0 cents, which renders as a zero monthly average rather than failing the whole account page. The rest of the behaviour (integer cents division over purchases flagged `in_current_month`) is unchanged, so the flag can be turned back on safely.

Also completed `Account.__init__`, which never stored `total_cents` / `total_this_month_cents`, so the attribute the summary reads did not exist.

Tests: added the case that was failing (an account with no current-month purchases now returns 0 instead of raising), alongside coverage of a shopper who did buy this month and one whose only purchases are from previous months.
input.summary: Return zero average spend when an account has no purchases in the current month instead of dividing by zero
